title: The 1935 Henderson personnel and the Roseland rivals
summary: Thomas names Benny Waters, George Stevenson, Thigpen and Max Merritt, before Roy and Chu joined, and describes Roseland, Benny Carter, Rex Stewart and Redman around Broadway in 1934.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, this band ... is the one with Roy Eldridge and Dick Vance Bench (?)?
No, they weren't there at that time.
This is the band with Benny Waters. Let me try to get the guys together now. The tenor, Benny Waters I think he's over in Europe now.

And George Stevenson, a fellow by the name of Thigpen trumpet player, Maddox Pigeon, a good one, too. A very good one. And Max Merritt ... Saxophone section was... I can't remember everybody. That's a long time ago, Stan.
Yeah. Well, this is before the band with Chu Berry and Roy in it?
Well, now that's the segue, '35 to '36. That's a direct segue right there. So, Snack had an idea. He had too many things going. He worked in Roseland, you know.

Oh, yeah. I worked in Roseland in '34. Benny Carter had his band across the street -- I can't remember the place -- and a very good band. Rex Stewart had a band over at the same place. Redman had that band at a place call the Congress.
Oh, there were like four ballrooms down there?

Oh, yeah. And, they had some nice things going there you know. And, after that I thought about these fellows in my way because I know I appreciate them as being great musicians. And it was my privilege to work with them.
